newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan May jobless rate at 2.51 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan May jobless rate at 2.51 percent.

text.p: Taiwan's unemployment rate was at 2.51 percent in May, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Monday.
The May jobless figure came in slightly below the average 2.65 percent forecast compiled from a June 20 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
It also was below April's rate of 2.59 percent.
All but one of the five economists polled had said they expected May joblessness to rise to varying degrees from April, due mainly to significant job losses on Taiwan's feedlots.
An islandwide outbreak of hog foot-and-mouth disease in late March forced a ban on pork exports, a US$1.5 billion business before the blight, and the slaughter of four million pigs.

Directorate economists explained that the effect of the farm epidemic was not as great as expected, since only a relatively small percentage of hog-related businesses shut down altogether, limiting job losses.
"Those affected were mostly slaughterhouses, big hog breeding companies, food processors and frozen meat businesses," directorate official Chen Chang-hsiung told reporters.
"Our figures show that only about 1,500 people from those businesses lost their jobs," Chen said.
Chen acknowledged that job losses on small pig farms were not included due to the difficulty of obtaining data.
A number of small farms had resumed hog breeding due to gradual resumption of domestic demand, he said.
Directorate officials said judging from the easing trend of joblessness in recent months, overall annual unemployment should be able to slow to reach a state target of 2.6 percent.
"It's quite likely we will be able to reach the target zone this year," Chen said.
For the first five months of 1997, the cumulative average jobless rate stood at 2.71 percent, officials said.
Joblessness in February was 2.97 percent, but edged down to 2.79 percent in April and 2.51 percent in May, the agency said.
The May unemployment figure not only was lower than the month-earlier level of 2.59 percent, but was the lowest in 12 months. Joblessness in May 1996 was 2.35 percent.
The number of unemployed in May fell to 236,000, down 6,000 from April.
Officials said the decline was due mainly to a steadily accelerating recovery, which had added jobs in the manufacturing and long-struggling construction sectors.
The number of employed rose 19,000 to 913,800 in May from April, but jobs in the agricultural sector dropped by 15,000, the agency said.
